correctness.rationale: The explicitly normalized R³ radial Fourier integral reduces to a sum of two shifted cubic-denominator terms. An exact integer-polynomial identity gives the rational density with a cubic P(s²). Its coefficient signs prove nonnegativity iff a²>=5ω²; if the constant term is negative, Descartes plus P(ω²)=a⁶ gives the unique simple positive sign-change root. Integrability justifies Fourier inversion and Bochner, and a.e.-positive density proves strictness. The full one-dimensional shifted Matérn spectrum is positive for every a>0, ω>=0. The actual standalone checker passed exact symbolic algebra and four independent radial quadrature comparisons. No finite tests are used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The canonical Matérn 3/2 correlation models differentiable spatial fields, while radial oscillation is a natural hole-effect modeling mechanism. Exact covariance admissibility is essential for legitimate Gram matrices. The theorem supplies a sharp, all-parameter three-dimensional damping/frequency threshold, strictness at equality, and the entire single low-frequency negative band when invalid; it also exposes a dimension-one versus dimension-three difference. These are natural structural facts, not an arbitrary finite computation or a generic Bochner restatement.
